clue.text: This game ends at twenty one

definitions.text: This game ends at twenty one

parts.words: This game ends at twenty one
parts.note: under the old scoring rules a game of ping-pong was won by the first player to reach twenty-one points, so a game ending there describes the sport

explanation.surface: A card game or darts match whose target score is twenty-one.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests pontoon (blackjack), where twenty-one is the magic total; the game meant is the bat-and-ball one, whose games went to 21 points until 2001.
explanation.definitionFit: A cryptic description of the sport through its traditional winning score of twenty-one points.

clue.text: Bank counters?

parts.note: read as the people at a bank who count money, rather than the counter tops of a bank

explanation.surface: The service counters in a high-street bank.
explanation.definitionFit: Bank cashiers who count out notes are traditionally called by this name, punning on counters as people who count.

clue.text: Leafy arbour in this section of New York ? Not quite!

indicators.note: not quite the whole word, so its final letter is dropped

parts.note: the Bowery is a street and neighbourhood in lower Manhattan

explanation.surface: A tourist wonders whether a shady garden seat belongs in a Manhattan district.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not quite!' trims the last letter, Y, from BOWERY.
explanation.definitionFit: A shady garden retreat formed by trees or climbing plants is a synonym for an arbour.

clue.text: The planes in turbulence are jumbos

indicators.note: turbulence throws the letters of the words the planes into disorder

explanation.surface: Aircraft buffeted by rough air are jumbo jets.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface makes jumbos the jets; here they are the large animals, the name coming from a famous zoo animal called Jumbo.
explanation.definitionFit: Jumbo is a common nickname for a large pachyderm, after the famous London Zoo animal.

clue.text: Tom Brown's chum, a card player ?

definitions.meaning: in Tom Brown's School Days, Harry ... is Tom's closest friend at Rugby School
in bridge the four players are named by compass points, one of them being the partner of West

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: the schoolfriend's surname, and the compass-point name of a bridge player.

clue.text: Lear's lines in moonshine

definitions.meaning: Edward Lear wrote famously absurd verse such as The Owl and the Pussy-cat
moonshine means foolish talk or rubbish

explanation.definitionFit: Lear's comic verse is the classic example of this genre, and moonshine is a synonym for rubbish talk.

clue.text: Hard hat, like this, on the head

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits on top, at the head of the second

parts.note: so means in this way, like this
lid is slang for a hat

explanation.surface: Advice to wear a hard hat placed on the head like so.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the head' puts SO above LID in this down entry; the hard hat of the surface is a red herring, 'Hard' alone being the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Firm and rigid, not soft or yielding, is a direct synonym of hard.

clue.text: Porcelain reddens when treated

indicators.note: treating the word reddens processes it into a new arrangement of letters

explanation.surface: A piece of china turns red when processed in a kiln.
explanation.definitionFit: Fine porcelain from Meissen near this German city is known by the city's name.

clue.text: Coaxing a little woman into embrace

indicators.note: into says the first pieces go inside the word for embrace

parts.note: to cling is to hold tight, to embrace
Jo March is one of the four sisters in Louisa May Alcott's Little Women

explanation.surface: Persuading a small wife into a hug.
explanation.walkthrough: 'little woman' is Jo March of Alcott's Little Women; 'into' is the container signal, and 'embrace' is a verb meaning hold tight, not the noun of the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Persuading by gentle flattery is a synonym of coaxing.

clue.text: Reduced salt when resort is least busy?

parts.note: reduced means cut down or low
to salt food is to season it

explanation.surface: A hotel cuts back on salt during its quiet months.
explanation.walkthrough: 'salt' is a verb here, flavouring food, not the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: The off-peak period of the year when a holiday destination has few visitors.

clue.text: The French hail-and-farewell

parts.note: le is a French word for the
ave is the Latin greeting meaning hail

explanation.surface: A French way of saying hello and goodbye.
explanation.walkthrough: AVE is the Latin salutation; the hyphenated phrase hides the split between hail (AVE) and farewell (the definition).
explanation.definitionFit: Taking one's leave means saying goodbye, so the word serves as a noun for farewell.

clue.text: Ground before end of July is rough

indicators.note: before puts the soil word ahead of the next piece

parts.note: ground means soil or earth

indicators.note: end of picks out the last letter of the next word

explanation.surface: Ground left until late July is rough and uneven.
explanation.definitionFit: Earthy humour is crude and coarse, so it shares the sense of rough or unrefined.

clue.text: Lifeless copse, would you say, an encumbrance ?

definitions.meaning: a fanciful literal reading: a copse is a small wood, and a lifeless one is a wood that has died
useless people or things that hold an organisation back

explanation.walkthrough: The printed 'cops' is surely 'copse', a small wood, which gives the playful literal reading.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: literally timber that has died, and figuratively the useless members holding a group back.

clue.text: Mo twinkling ?

definitions.meaning: mo is informal for a moment, as in half a mo
a twinkling is an instant, as in the twinkling of an eye

explanation.definitionFit: Both are informal words for a very brief moment, the sixtieth part of a minute.

clue.text: Well-known climber in exotic climates

indicators.note: exotic suggests something strange and foreign, so the letters of climates are made unfamiliar

explanation.surface: A famous mountaineer in faraway climates.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exotic' rearranges CLIMATES; the climber is a plant, not a mountaineer.
explanation.definitionFit: This popular garden plant climbs walls and trellises, so it is a well-known climber.

clue.text: Tongue of schoolboy, swallowing last of cherries

indicators.note: swallowing means taking another piece inside

parts.note: an Etonian is a pupil at Eton College, an English public school

indicators.note: last of picks out the final letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A schoolboy's tongue as he gulps down cherries.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swallowing' puts S, the last letter of 'cherries', inside ETONIAN; ETON is a famous English boarding school.
explanation.definitionFit: Tongue means language, and this is the language of a Baltic state.

clue.text: Mr Chips was such a great painter

definitions.meaning: Mr Chips, of Goodbye, Mr Chips, was an elderly schoolteacher
an eminent European artist of the period before about 1800

explanation.definitionFit: Read literally, an aged schoolteacher; as a fixed term, a great painter of the past or his work.

clue.text: Chateau workers, first-class people in Australia

definitions.meaning: people who fill bottles with wine at a French vineyard estate
in Australian slang a bottler is an excellent person or thing

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: people who bottle wine, and the Australian slang for outstanding people.

clue.text: Great dislike of a translation

parts.note: a version is a rendering of a text into another language

explanation.surface: Strong distaste for a translated text.
explanation.definitionFit: A strong feeling of distaste or antipathy is a direct synonym of great dislike.

clue.text: The south wind, over Egypt, is severe

indicators.note: in a down clue over places the wind above the next piece

parts.note: Auster is the Latin name of the south wind
E is taken as a short abbreviation for Egypt, its initial letter

explanation.surface: A harsh southerly wind blows across Egypt.
explanation.walkthrough: AUSTER is the classical south wind; 'over' sets it above E (Egypt) in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Stern, plain and harsh in manner or style means the same as severe.

clue.text: Proverbs, these days, take a very long time

parts.note: AD, anno domini, marks the present era
ages means a very long time, as in waiting for ages

explanation.surface: Old sayings that take forever to say nowadays.
explanation.definitionFit: Traditional short sayings expressing a truth are proverbs.

clue.text: Looked daggers at son, dressed like a monk

parts.note: a monk wears a hooded cowl, so dressed like one is cowled

explanation.surface: A parent glares at a son who has turned up in a monk's habit.
explanation.definitionFit: To look daggers is to glare angrily, which is what frowning fiercely means.

clue.text: Bath, we hear, showing such meagreness

indicators.note: we hear says the phrase is spoken, giving a sound-alike

parts.note: Bath in Somerset is the famous English spa city, built round Roman baths

explanation.surface: Someone notes how thinly supplied the bath water is.
explanation.walkthrough: Bath is an English city famous for its spa; 'spa city' said in a non-rhotic British accent sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Scantiness or thinness of supply is what meagreness means.

clue.text: Pole in personnel

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: a long stick carried in the hand, and the workforce of an organisation.

clue.text: A cough troubled this cowboy

indicators.note: troubled means disturbed, so the letters of a cough are stirred up

explanation.surface: A cowboy is afflicted by a nagging cough.
explanation.definitionFit: This South American horseman of the pampas is the local equivalent of a cowboy.

clue.text: Copper taking fresh air in papal court

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

indicators.note: fresh suggests the word air is made anew in a different order

explanation.surface: A policeman gets some fresh air at the Vatican.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fresh' rearranges AIR to RIA; copper is the metal, not a policeman.
explanation.definitionFit: The body of departments through which the Pope governs the Church is the papal court.

clue.text: Money taken from chapel funds

indicators.note: taken from says the letters are lifted out of the run of words that follow

explanation.surface: Cash removed from a church's collection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken from' picks out the run inside 'chapel funds'.
explanation.definitionFit: An old, mildly disparaging word for money, especially ill-gotten wealth.

clue.text: Girl from the US taking the morning off

indicators.note: off says the morning letters are removed from the country

parts.note: America is the usual name for the United States
AM, ante meridiem, means the morning

explanation.surface: An American girl takes the morning off work.
explanation.definitionFit: A girl's name, the kind of first name a crossword clue can call simply a girl.

clue.text: Sort of roll. (, A-E, etc)?

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held 'Sort of roll. (, A-E, etc)?' is garbled: the bracket begins with a stray comma and a character or symbol is missing; no scan or search recovers the printed clue.

clue.text: Speedy striker, perhaps, in state of urgency

parts.note: speedy means fast
a striker in football is an example of a forward, an attacking player

explanation.surface: A quick centre-forward plays with great urgency.
explanation.walkthrough: The football surface hides a phrase from tape and video players: fast-forward means winding on at speed, which suggests haste.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in fast-forward is a figurative idiom for rushing at speed, as when things are pressing.
